objective: I can practice putting things back. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Using the borrowed-things log from an earlier lesson, or a quick list made today of items currently out of place, the learner gathers each item, names its correct owner or spot out loud, and physically returns it while a trusted adult watches and checks off each completed return.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult directly observes and confirms that each item actually reaches its owner or storage spot, not just that the learner reports it happened.

simulationAlternative.description: If there is no borrowed item on hand this week, the learner instead writes, in specific detail, exactly where each of three real belongings in their space would be returned to (the owner, the room, and the shelf or drawer) and explains the return step for each one.

materials: learner-local: the borrowed-things log or a quick list of out-of-place items

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Describe one specific difference you notice in your space now that every borrowed item is returned, and name one thing that will make returning items easier next time.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Return accuracy: Every item on the list is returned to its exact owner or storage spot, confirmed by the adult present. | Naming before placing: The learner states out loud where each item belongs before placing it, for every item. | Adult-confirmed completion: The adult directly observes and confirms each return in the moment it happens. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner set up a standing return spot near the exit door so the next batch of borrowed items gets returned the same day they are noticed, instead of piling up first.

duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: putting things back worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Using the borrowed-things log from an earlier lesson, or a quick list made today of items currently out of place, the learner gathers each item, names its correct owner or spot out loud, and physically returns it while a trusted adult watches and checks off each completed return.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact putting things back decision or action.
Model move 2: Before returning anything, gather every item that needs to go back today.
Model move 3: With your adult watching, return each item one at a time.

Model check: Return accuracy: Every item on the list is returned to its exact owner or storage spot, confirmed by the adult present. | Naming before placing: The learner states out loud where each item belongs before placing it, for every item. | Adult-confirmed completion: The adult directly observes and confirms each return in the moment it happens.

resources.title: putting things back action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for putting things back.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-guided-card.

5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: putting things back coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Using the borrowed-things log from an earlier lesson, or a quick list made today of items currently out of place, the learner gathers each item, names its correct owner or spot out loud, and physically returns it while a trusted adult watches and checks off each completed return.
Coach direction: Before returning anything, gather every item that needs to go back today.
Learner prompt: List every item you are about to return today.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: putting things back complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult watching, return each item one at a time. Say where it belongs before you move it, then place it exactly there.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I said out loud where each item belongs before moving it.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I carried and placed each item in its exact spot, not just somewhere nearby.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I handed items directly to a person if the item belongs to a person rather than a shelf.
Response 4 (t2-p4): My adult watched and confirmed each return before I moved to the next item.

Equal-access rule: If there is no borrowed item on hand this week, the learner instead writes, in specific detail, exactly where each of three real belongings in their space would be returned to (the owner, the room, and the shelf or drawer) and explains the return step for each one.

resources.title: putting things back minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Describe one specific difference you notice in your space now that every borrowed item is returned, and name one thing that will make returning items easier next time.

Success checks: Return accuracy: Every item on the list is returned to its exact owner or storage spot, confirmed by the adult present. | Naming before placing: The learner states out loud where each item belongs before placing it, for every item. | Adult-confirmed completion: The adult directly observes and confirms each return in the moment it happens.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: putting things back supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional putting things back condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Return accuracy: Every item on the list is returned to its exact owner or storage spot, confirmed by the adult present. | Naming before placing: The learner states out loud where each item belongs before placing it, for every item. | Adult-confirmed completion: The adult directly observes and confirms each return in the moment it happens..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u05-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

realRoute.title: putting things back — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Do not begin the physical action until a household-authorized guardian gives permission and is available for the supervision or review named in this lesson.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
With your adult watching, return each item one at a time. Say where it belongs before you move it, then place it exactly there.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record; only the household-authorized guardian attests that the named physical action occurred.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
